rules.description: AI-overused vocabulary, 2023 to mid-2024 (GPT-4) bucket. Scored by density and co-occurrence, never by a single hit: one or two hits may be coincidence, but these words cluster. 'key' is matched only in its importance-adjective position to spare 'API key' and 'XOR key'.
rules.source_citation: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § High density of "AI vocabulary" words, 2023 to mid-2024 bucket

positive: The report delves into an intricate tapestry of tradecraft, a testament to the evolving landscape.
negative: The malware reads the XOR key from its config and decrypts the API key store.

rules.description: AI-overused vocabulary, mid-2024 to mid-2025 (GPT-4o) bucket. Overlaps the GPT-4 bucket on purpose because the guide's lists overlap; the era estimator disambiguates on distinctive terms.
rules.source_citation: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § High density of "AI vocabulary" words, mid-2024 to mid-2025 bucket

positive: This approach aligns with best practices, fostering resilience and showcasing the team's depth while highlighting key wins.
negative: The patch changed the parser. Nothing else moved.

rules.description: AI-overused vocabulary, mid-2025 onward (GPT-5) bucket: the list narrows to emphasizing, enhance, highlighting, showcasing. Notability-claim language is covered by the canned-notability category. Era estimator calls gpt5 only when this narrowed set fires without earlier-era distinctive terms.
rules.source_citation: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § High density of "AI vocabulary" words, mid-2025 onward bucket

positive: Enhancing coverage while showcasing results and highlighting the approach, emphasizing outcomes.
negative: The actor pivoted to a second C2 within an hour.

rules.description: Grok-idiosyncratic vocabulary: causal, empirical, correlate, plus continued overuse of underscore as of 2026.
rules.source_citation: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § High density of "AI vocabulary" words, Grok notes

positive: The empirical data correlate with a causal link, underscoring the empirical trend.
negative: The beacon interval was 300 seconds with 20 percent jitter.

rules.description: AI-overused vocabulary of the 2025-2026 chat models (Claude 4.x, GPT-5, Gemini 3): genuinely, nuanced, load-bearing, compelling, seamless, profound, transformative, holistic, paramount, multifaceted, invaluable, myriad, plethora, symphony, demystify, unleash, unveil, 'at its core', 'at the forefront', 'deceptively simple', 'heavy lifting', 'a lot to unpack', 'quiet confidence'. Security-domain collisions are excluded on purpose: 'beacon' (C2), 'realm' (Kerberos), 'unlock' (devices), 'harness' (test harness), 'elevate' (privileges) only match in their figurative frames. Feeds the chat2026 era bucket together with the narrative pattern categories.
rules.source_citation: Polytranslator, Claude-speak: 'genuinely', 'nuanced', 'load-bearing'; Olivia Cal, AI words blacklist 2026: 'Demystify', 'Symphony', 'Myriad', 'Plethora', 'Unleash', 'At its core'; Forbes (2026-02-03): 'quiet' everywhere; stopslop 2.1 observed corpus
rules.pattern: \b(?:genuinely|nuanced?|load-bearing|compelling|seamless(?:ly)?|navigat(?:e|es|ing) the (?:complexities|landscape|nuances)|the realm of|embark(?:s|ed|ing)? on|elevat(?:e|es|ed|ing) (?:the|your|their|our) (?:experience|understanding|game|work|approach|conversation)|empower(?:s|ed|ing)?|unlock(?:s|ed|ing)? (?:deeper|new|the (?:full|true)|insights?|value|potential|opportunities)|harness(?:es|ed|ing)? the (?:power|potential|full)|cultivat(?:e|es|ed|ing)|streamlin(?:e|es|ed|ing)|resonat(?:e|es|ed|ing)|profound(?:ly)?|transformative|holistic(?:ally)?|paramount|multifaceted|invaluable|myriad|plethora|symphony|demystif(?:y|ies|ied|ying)|unleash(?:es|ed|ing)?|unveil(?:s|ed|ing)?|at its core|at the forefront|deceptively simple|heavy lifting|a lot to unpack|quiet(?:ly)? (?:confidence|truth|rebellion|power|revolution|shift|brilliance|competence|reliability|strength))\b

positive: Genuinely, the nuanced answer is that this deceptively simple gate does the heavy lifting, a transformative and multifaceted design.
negative: The Cobalt Strike beacon checked in every 300 seconds. The Kerberos realm was misconfigured, so the operator could unlock the device and elevate privileges.

rules.description: Claude-idiosyncratic vocabulary (Claude 4.x through Opus 5, 2025-2026), the per-model bucket the guide's 'Differences between LLMs' section calls for. Anchored on 'load-bearing', the strongest quantified narrative tell in the literature: in a 461k GitHub pull-request corpus it appears 929 times inside the Claude-authored cluster against 82 outside it. Runners-up: 'the seam', 'the tell', 'the unlock', 'carry the argument', 'earns its keep', 'doing the work', 'hand-waving', 'different physics', 'lands hardest', 'worth sitting with', plus consultant register ('double-click on', 'pressure-test', 'north star'). 'surface' as a verb and 'beacon' are deliberately excluded: both are ordinary SOC vocabulary and would fire on every hunt writeup.
rules.source_citation: louisabraham/load-bearing, the load-bearing vocabulary of Claude (461k PR corpus, 929 in-cluster vs 82 out); claudisms.ai, a living banlist of AI-writing tells; explainx.ai, Claude Opus 5 Claudisms (2026-08); Ivo Velitchkov, 22 Claude Cliches (2026-06-25); Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing § Differences between LLMs
rules.pattern: \b(?:load-bearing|the (?:seam|tell|unlock)\b|carry the argument|earns its keep|doing the (?:real )?work here|hand-?waving|reflexive hedging|different physics|lands hardest|worth sitting with|the line I keep coming back to|double-click(?:ing)? on|pressure-test(?:ing|ed)?|north star)\b

positive: That gate is load-bearing. The seam is the tell, and the unlock is that it earns its keep without hand-waving.
negative: The attack surface is large. Analysts surface findings weekly, and the beacon interval was 300 seconds.
